topic: Year-end tax moves with a Dec 31, 2026 cutoff

headline: Four tax moves that end on *Dec. 31*

items.title: Equipment: in service, not just bought
items.text: To deduct it for 2026, it must be ready and available for use by Dec. 31.

items.title: Charity without itemizing
items.text: New for 2026: up to $1,000 of cash gifts ($2,000 joint). Give by Dec. 31.

ig_caption:
Most 2026 tax moves stop counting on December 31. Save this before the holidays get busy.

✔️ Equipment: buying it is not enough. It has to be placed in service, ready and available for use, by Dec. 31 to count for 2026.
✔️ Charity: new for 2026, you can deduct up to $1,000 of cash gifts ($2,000 filing jointly) even if you take the standard deduction.
✔️ 401(k): the 2026 deferral limit is $24,500, plus $8,000 if you are 50 or older. Raise your payroll deferral before the last paychecks of the year.
✔️ Then mark January 15, 2027 for the fourth-quarter estimated tax payment.

li_caption:
Most tax-saving moves for 2026 have a hard cutoff of December 31. After that, there is nothing to fix in March.

Four we review with owners every year-end:

1. Equipment. Buying it is not the test. It has to be placed in service, meaning ready and available for its intended use, by December 31 to be deducted for 2026. A machine delivered in December and installed in January counts for 2027.
2. Charity without itemizing. Starting in 2026, non-itemizers can deduct up to $1,000 of cash gifts to qualifying charities, or $2,000 filing jointly. Keep the bank record or written acknowledgment.
3. 401(k) payroll deferrals. The 2026 limit is $24,500, plus an $8,000 catch-up at 50 or older. Deferrals come out of paychecks, so the change has to be in before the last payroll of the year.
4. Then mark January 15, 2027, when the fourth-quarter 2026 estimated tax payment is due.
